sections.title: The Arrest of Jesus
observations: In this section, we witness the betrayal of Jesus by Judas Iscariot. Judas' actions are prophesied in Scripture, reminding us that God’s plan includes even the darkest human actions.
The characters involved—the religious leaders and Judas—demonstrate the lengths to which humanity will go to reject God, contrasting starkly with Jesus' unwavering commitment to his mission.

sections.title: The Last Supper
observations: Jesus shares a final meal with his disciples, establishing the Lord's Supper, which becomes a central sacrament in Christian worship.
The symbolism of bread and wine represents the body and blood of Christ, emphasizing sacrifice and communion with believers.

sections.title: Jesus Predicts Peter's Denial
observations: Here, Jesus foretells Peter's denial, highlighting not only Peter’s vulnerability but also Jesus' foreknowledge and grace.
This moment serves as a reminder of human weakness in the face of trial and the need for divine strength.

sections.title: Gethsemane: The Agony of the Garden
observations: Jesus prays earnestly in Gethsemane, revealing his humanity and the emotional weight of his mission. This section illustrates the tension between Jesus’ desire for the cup to pass and his submission to the Father’s will.
The disciples’ inability to stay awake reflects a broader theme of spiritual dullness in humanity.

sections.title: Jesus' Arrest
observations: The events of Jesus’ arrest unfold swiftly, culminating in betrayal by one of his own disciples and the violence of the crowds. This emphasizes the chaos of sin and the unwavering sovereign plan of God in the face of rebellion.
Peter's impulse to fight reveals the struggle between divine purpose and human instinct.

sections.title: Jesus Before the Sanhedrin
observations: Jesus is condemned by his own people, demonstrating a profound rejection of truth and righteousness. His silence before his accusers speaks volumes about his identity as the sacrificial lamb.
This trial is a pivotal moment where prophetic fulfillment and human rebellion collide.

importantVerses.commentary: ‘This is my body, which is for you,’ emphasizes the sacrificial nature of Jesus' mission and the establishment of a new covenant.
‘Abba, Father, all things are possible for you; remove this cup from me,’ reveals the human nature of Jesus and the profound struggle he faced.
‘You have heard the blasphemy!’ shows the seriousness of the charges against Jesus, illustrating humanity’s rejection of the true nature of God.

questions: What does the betrayal of Judas teach us about sin and its consequences?
How does the institution of the Lord's Supper shape our understanding of communion today?
In what ways can we relate to the disciples in their moments of weakness during Jesus' arrest?
What can Jesus' prayer in Gethsemane teach us about submission to God's will in our own lives?
How does the conduct of Jesus during his trial inform our understanding of justice and truth?
